entries.subject: Disc-resolved images or interferometry of WASP-43
entries.finding: At 87.15 pc a 0.665 solar-radius star spans 0.071 mas (computed from the radius and distance), far below the resolution of any telescope or optical interferometer. No image or interferometric diameter is published.
entries.revisitWhen: An interferometric diameter or surface image of WASP-43 is published.

entries.subject: Stellar radius and mass from Challener et al. (2024)
entries.finding: Table 1 lists the assumed stellar radius 0.665 solar radii and mass 0.6916 solar masses, matching Hammond et al. (2024); they set the sphere and the display GM, and the WASP-43b package's orbit is expressed in this radius.

entries.subject: Gaia EDR3 astrometry via SIMBAD
entries.finding: Position, parallax 11.474 +/- 0.016 mas (87.15 pc, no zero-point correction) and proper motion -41.992, -38.004 mas/yr from Gaia EDR3; radial velocity -3.7 +/- 0.7 km/s from Gaia DR2.

entries.subject: Spin axis of WASP-43
entries.finding: Esposito et al. (2017, A&A 601, A53) measured the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect of WASP-43b with HARPS-N: sky-projected obliquity 3.5 +/- 6.8 degrees, aligned. The rotation record takes the pole from WASP-43b's orbit normal (cssearth-orbit-aligned-pole@1) with longitude 0 facing the Sun. The rotation period is measured, 15.6 +/- 0.4 days (Hellier et al. 2011), but with no prime meridian no spin is shown.

entries.subject: A measured optical spectrum for the photosphere colour
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 published no BP/RP (XP) spectrum for WASP-43 (source_id 3767805209112436736, has_xp_sampled and has_xp_continuous false), so no flux-calibrated optical spectrum is available to integrate.
entries.revisitWhen: Gaia DR4 publishes XP spectra, or a flux-calibrated optical spectrum of WASP-43 is released.

entries.subject: Photosphere colour from the Gaia DR3 photometric temperature
entries.finding: GSP-Phot gives 4,416 K (16th–84th percentiles 4,407–4,424 K; systematics not included). A Planck spectrum at that temperature through the CIE 1931 2° observer gives sRGB 255, 220, 184 (#ffdcb8); the percentiles move a channel by at most 1. The spectroscopic 4,520 K that Challener et al. (2024) use gives 255, 222, 189. A blackbody ignores the K dwarf's absorption bands, and the colour carries no brightness.

entries.subject: Tilt of WASP-43's spin axis along the line of sight
entries.finding: The Rossiter-McLaughlin effect fixes the spin axis's angle on the sky, not its inclination toward the observer. The pole is taken to share the orbit's 82 degree inclination, and that is supported: Esposito et al. (2017) combine the measured rotation period, 15.6 +/- 0.4 days (Hellier et al. 2011), with the star's radius and v sin i to get sin I = 1.08 +/- 0.25, an inclination above 72 degrees at 68% confidence. The orbit's own position angle on the sky is a display convention, which the axis inherits.

entries.subject: Limb darkening measured from TESS transits
entries.finding: Patel & Espinoza (2022, AJ 163, 228; VizieR J/AJ/163/228 table 4) fitted a quadratic law to TESS transits of WASP-43b: u1 0.55 (+0.22 -0.31), u2 0.00 (+0.46 -0.30), so the limb is 45% as bright as the centre (about 25 to 80% within the uncertainty). The row is pinned and drawn as the colour lens's limb plate. TESS covers 600-1000 nm; no visible-light measurement exists. The JWST transits in the WASP-43b package also constrain limb darkening, but in the infrared, where it is weaker.

entries.subject: Starspots on WASP-43
entries.finding: Esposito et al. (2017) find enhanced Ca II H and K emission, so the star is magnetically active and has spots, but no spot map exists or can be made with current data: the 0.07 mas disc cannot be imaged, the slow rotation rules out Doppler imaging, and a spot crossed during a transit is one strip at one moment while spots evolve over days. Recorded as a note on the lens, not drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: A published spot map or spot-crossing mapping of WASP-43.

entries.subject: Distant marker for WASP-43
entries.finding: The marker is the colour lens as a disc with the measured TESS limb darkening, rendered from the pinned colour and limb-darkening records; it replaced the scaffold's flat disc.
